question_html: Which book of accounts is known as the principal book of account where all accounts (personal, real, and nominal) are maintained?

options.A: Cash Book
options.B: Journal

answer_html: Answer: (C) Ledger is known as the principal book of account which contains all sets of accounts[cite: 56].

question_html: What is the primary function of a Ledger in accounting?

options.A: To record transactions chronologically
options.B: To classify and group original transactions into individual accounts

answer_html: Answer: (B) After recording original transactions in the journal, entries are classified and grouped by preparing accounts in the ledger[cite: 56].

question_html: How many sides does a standard ledger account have?

options.A: One side
options.B: Two sides (Debit and Credit)

answer_html: Answer: (B) A ledger account has two sides - debit (left side) and credit (right side)[cite: 56].

question_html: Which of the following columns is NOT part of a standard ledger account structure?

options.A: Date
options.B: Particulars

answer_html: Answer: (D) The standard columns in each side of a ledger account are Date, Particulars, Journal Folio (J.F.), and Amount[cite: 56].

question_html: What does 'J.F.' stand for in a ledger account?

options.A: Journal Folio
options.B: Ledger Folio

answer_html: Answer: (A) J.F. stands for Journal Folio, representing the page from where entries are taken for posting[cite: 56].

question_html: The process of transferring debit and credit items from the journal to classified accounts in the ledger is called:

options.A: Journalizing
options.B: Posting

answer_html: Answer: (B) The process of transferring debit and credit items from journal to classified accounts in the ledger is known as posting[cite: 56].
topic_text: Rules of Posting from Journal to Ledger

question_html: In ledger posting, which word is traditionally used in the particular column for accounts written on the debit side?

options.A: By
options.B: To

answer_html: Answer: (B) The word 'To' is used in the particulars column with accounts written on the debit side[cite: 56].
topic_text: Use of 'To' and 'By' in Ledger Posting

question_html: In ledger posting, which word is used in the particulars column with accounts written on the credit side?

options.A: To
options.B: By

answer_html: Answer: (B) The word 'By' is used with the accounts written in the particular column of the credit side[cite: 56].
topic_text: Use of 'To' and 'By' in Ledger Posting

question_html: Do the words 'To' and 'By' used in ledger accounts have any independent literal meaning regarding debits and credits?

options.A: Yes, they indicate direction of cash flow
options.B: No, they do not have any intrinsic meanings but are convention used to designate debited and credited accounts
options.C: Yes, 'To' means increase and 'By' means decrease
options.D: Yes, they represent personal and real accounts respectively

answer_html: Answer: (B) 'To' and 'By' do not have any meanings but are used to designate the account debited and credited[cite: 56].
topic_text: Use of 'To' and 'By' in Ledger Posting

question_html: When balancing an account, if the credit side total is greater than the debit side total, the difference is known as:

options.A: Debit balance
options.B: Credit balance

answer_html: Answer: (B) If the credit side is bigger than the debit side, it is a credit balance[cite: 56].
topic_text: Balancing an Account and Carry Down/Brought Down

question_html: How is a credit balance inserted on the debit side to make both sides equal when balancing an account?

options.A: By Balance c/d
options.B: To Balance c/d

answer_html: Answer: (B) The credit balance is written on the debit side as 'To Balance c/d' (carried down)[cite: 56].
topic_text: Balancing an Account and Carry Down/Brought Down

question_html: What does 'c/d' stand for in ledger balancing?

options.A: Current Date
options.B: Carried Down

answer_html: Answer: (B) c/d stands for 'carried down'[cite: 56].
topic_text: Balancing an Account and Carry Down/Brought Down

question_html: What does 'b/d' stand for when bringing down an opening balance for a new period?

options.A: Brought Down
options.B: Business Debit

answer_html: Answer: (A) b/d stands for 'brought down'[cite: 56].
topic_text: Balancing an Account and Carry Down/Brought Down

question_html: Which of the following accounts are NOT balanced at the end of an accounting period?

options.A: Personal accounts
options.B: Real accounts

answer_html: Answer: (C) Nominal accounts are not balanced; their ending balances are transferred to the profit and loss account[cite: 56].
topic_text: Treatment of Nominal Accounts at Year End

question_html: Where are the balances of nominal accounts transferred at the end of the accounting period?

options.A: Balance Sheet
options.B: Profit and Loss Account

answer_html: Answer: (B) Nominal accounts are not balanced; the balances in the end are transferred to the profit and loss account[cite: 56].
topic_text: Treatment of Nominal Accounts at Year End

question_html: In ledger posting, if an account is debited in the journal, how should it be posted in the ledger account? (Scenario 16)

options.A: Debited with the reference of the respective credit account
options.B: Credited with the reference of the debit account

answer_html: Answer: (A) The concerned account debited in the journal should also be debited in the ledger with reference to the respective credit account[cite: 56].

question_html: In preparing a stationery account, if opening inventory is ₹480, purchases by cheque ₹800, and purchases on credit ₹1,280, what is the total before balancing (Illustration 1)? (Scenario 17)
answer_html: Answer: (A) Total on the debit side is 480 + 800 + 1,280 = ₹2,560[cite: 56].

question_html: How are opening debit balances brought forward in a ledger account for a new period? (Scenario 18)

options.A: By Balance b/d on the credit side
options.B: To Balance b/d on the debit side
options.C: To Balance c/d on the debit side
options.D: By Balance c/d on the credit side

answer_html: Answer: (B) Debit balance is written on the debit side as 'To Balance b/d' as the opening balance[cite: 56].

question_html: Which accounts are ultimately reflected in the Balance Sheet at the end of the accounting period? (Scenario 19)

options.A: Only nominal accounts
options.B: Only personal and real accounts

answer_html: Answer: (B) Only personal and real accounts balances are ultimately shown in the balance sheet at the end of the accounting period[cite: 56].

question_html: How is the Capital account adjusted at the end of the accounting period? (Scenario 20)

options.A: For profit or loss (net of nominal accounts)
options.B: By transferring cash directly to reserves
options.D: By creating a separate suspense account

answer_html: Answer: (A) The capital account is adjusted for profit or loss (i.e. net of nominal accounts) at the end of the accounting period[cite: 56].
